workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(docker): initialize plugin daemon storage permissions. Target files: docker/docker-compose-template.yaml, docker/docker-compose.yaml. Since plugin daemon 0.6.12 the container runs as the `dify` user (uid 1001), but `./volumes/plugin_daemon` is created by Docker as root on a fresh install, and on upgraded installs it still holds files written by the old root daemon. So plugin installs fail with `mkdir /app/storage/assets: permission denied`. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/45615)

workarounds.symptom: parse_and_check_json_markdown raises TypeError (or silently passes validation) on non-dict LLM output
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(libs): reject non-dict output in parse_and_check_json_markdown. Target files: api/libs/json_in_md_parser.py, api/tests/unit_tests/libs/test_json_in_md_parser.py. `parse_and_check_json_markdown` in `api/libs/json_in_md_parser.py` only special-cases `list` results before running the `key not in json_obj` check, so non-dict objects leak into it with two wrong behaviours: (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/45225)

workarounds.symptom: parse_time_range mishandles DST spring-forward gaps that aren't exactly one hour (crashes on >1h gaps, wrong instant on <1h gaps)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(api): correct DST spring-forward handling in parse_time_range. Target files: api/libs/datetime_utils.py, api/tests/unit_tests/libs/test_datetime_utils.py. `libs/datetime_utils.py::parse_time_range` resolved a non-existent (DST spring-forward) wall-clock time by adding a hardcoded one hour, assuming every gap is exactly one hour. Real tzdata has other gap sizes, producing two bugs: (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/39231)

workarounds.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the f
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **A plugin could exhaust worker memory with one declared number.** The blob chunk merger pre-allocated a buffer of the plugin-declared total length before checking it against the file size limit, so a plugin claiming an absurd size crashed the worker with `MemoryError` — the 30 MB limit was never consulted. The declared size is now validated first and rejected with the documented size-limit error. (#42021). Upstream PR #42021. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/42021)

workarounds.symptom: dify 1.17.1: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built
workarounds.workaround: Fix: **Any PDF loaded from a URL crashed with a bare `AssertionError`.** After tenant context was added to the PDF extractor, the code path used by `load_from_url` — including the built-in web scraper whenever a target returns `Content-Type: application/pdf` — asserted on an upload record that URL loads never have. Tenant context is now optional, image extraction is skipped when it is absent, and text extraction works again. (#41950). Upstream PR #41950. (Ref: https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/41950)
